1  THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal arises out of the judgment and award dated 28.11.2018 in M.V.C.No.268/2018 by Additional Senior Civil Judge and MACT XIII, Madhugiri.
2. By consent of both sides the appeal is taken up for final disposal though the matter is posted for orders.

3. Heard learned counsel appearing for the appellant and respondent.
4.

The petition is filed by the claimant under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act 1998, claiming compensation on account of the death of deceased Chandrappa in road traffic accident dated 15.01.2018 at 7.30 a.m.

It was contended that while the deceased was proceeding from his village to Medigeshi on Madhugiri Pavagada road, a KSRTC bus bearing No.KA-06-F-1214 dashed against his moped and as a result he fell down and sustained fatal injuries and died while being treated in the hospital.
5.

The petitioners before the Tribunal contended that the deceased Chandrappa was aged about 55 years at the time of his death and he was earning `30,000/- per month by milk vending and other business and he used to maintain his entire family.

They also contended that the concerned police had registered a case in Crime No.2/2018 against the driver of the bus and the accident was due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
6. On being issued with the notice by the Tribunal, the respondent-KSRTC appeared and filed objections denying the negligence on the part of the driver of the bus.
7. On the basis of the pleadings, the Tribunal framed necessary issues.

In order to prove their case,
the petitioner No.1 was examined herself as PW-1 and one witness was examined as PW-2 and 9 documents as per Ex.P1 to Ex.P9 were marked on their side.
The respondent - KSRTC examined the driver as RW-1 and no documents were marked.

8. The Tribunal after appreciation of the evidence available and also by applying the guidelines issued by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Pranay Sethi1, a compensation of `6,46,000/- was arrived at by adopting a multiplier of 9 and taking the notional income of (2017) 16 SCC 680 the deceased to be `8,000/- per month.

sentences.text: Learned counsel appearing for the appellant would submit that the income of the deceased taken at `8,000/- per month do not confirm to the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority (hereinafter referred to as 'KSLSA' for short) for settlement of the case before the Lokadalat and also do not confirm to the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.

Secondly, he fairly submits that the age of the deceased was taken at 65 years at the time of the death and relevant multiplier was 7.
11.

However, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent submits that the notional income of the deceased taken at `8,000/- per month need not be varied and the criteria for settlement of dispute before the Lokadalat cannot be made to apply to the proceedings in Court.
12.
On perusal of the impugned judgment passed by the Tribunal, it is evident that the Tribunal has accepted the age of the deceased to be 65 years as may be found in para 17 of the judgment.
Therefore, the appropriate multiplier would have been 7 and not 9.
Secondly, insofar as the income of the deceased is concerned, there are no documentary evidence available on record to prove the same.

In umpteen number of cases, this Court has adopted the notional income as suggested by the KSLSA for the disposal of the cases before the Lokadalat and also held that such guidelines by KSLSA is in general conformity with the wages fixed under the Minimum Wages Act.
Therefore, the income of the deceased should have been taken at `12,500/- instead of `8,000/- per month.

13. Under these circumstances, by deducting 1/3 of the income towards the personal expenses of the deceased and adopting a multiplier of 7 as the deceased was aged 65 years, the loss of dependency would be `7,00,000/- (`12,500x12x2/3x7).
14. Insofar as, the consortium is concerned, the Tribunal has awarded a sum of `40,000/- only even though there are 4 dependants the deceased.
The claimants are the wife and the children of the deceased.

Therefore, each of them are entitled for a sum of `44,000/- and, as such, a sum of `1,76,000/- is awarded under this head, by relying on the decision in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v/s Nanu Ram Alias Chuhru Ram2.

Thus petitioners are entitled for a sum of `9,09,000/-
under following heads.

Consortium
The Tribunal has awarded the compensation amount only to the claimant No.1 which cannot be justified.

All (2018) 18 SCC 130 the claimants are also entitled for the compensation and therefore,
the appeal has to be allowed in part.
Hence, the following:-
ORDER i. The appeal is allowed-in-part.
ii. The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified holding that the claimants are entitled for a total compensation of `9,09,000/- instead of sum of `6,46,000/- awarded by the Tribunal.

iii. The Sharadamma vs The Managing Director on 22 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/187043985/
3 claimants are also entitled for the interest on the enhanced compensation amount excluding the delayed period of 233 days.

the petitioner No.1 is entitled for 70% of the compensation amount.
The claimant Nos.2, 3 and 4 are entitled for 10% of the total compensation amount.
v. The respondent is directed to deposit the compensation amount within six weeks from the date of this order.
